text: It was four oclock in the morning. <break time="0.8s" /> When someone knocked. <break time="0.8s" /> At the street door. <break time="0.8s" /> Three police officers. <break time="0.8s" /> Came in very politely. <break time="0.8s" /> A neighbor had heard a scream. <break time="0.8s" /> During the night. <break time="0.8s" /> And they had come. <break time="0.8s" /> To search the house. <break time="0.8s" /> I smiled. <break time="0.8s" /> For what had I to fear. <break time="0.8s" /> I told them. <break time="0.8s" /> The scream was my own. <break time="0.8s" /> In a dream. <break time="0.8s" /> I brought chairs. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the old mans room. <break time="0.8s" /> And placed my own chair. <break time="0.8s" /> Right above the boards. <break time="0.8s" /> The officers were satisfied. <break time="0.8s" /> And we talked happily. <break time="0.8s" /> About ordinary things. <break time="0.8s" /> But soon I felt myself. <break time="0.8s" /> Getting pale. <break time="0.8s" /> And I wished them gone. <break time="0.8s" /> A ringing began in my ears. <break time="0.8s" /> A low, dull, quick sound. <break time="0.8s" /> Much like a watch. <break time="0.8s" /> Wrapped in cotton. <break time="0.8s" /> It grew louder and louder. <break time="0.8s" /> But the officers chatted pleasantly. <break time="0.8s" /> And smiled. <break time="0.8s" /> Was it possible. <break time="0.8s" /> They did not hear it. <break time="0.8s" /> No, no. <break time="0.8s" /> They heard. <break time="0.8s" /> And they were making fun of my terror. <break time="0.8s" /> I could bear those smiles. <break time="0.8s" /> No longer. <break time="0.8s" /> And I felt that I must scream or die. <break time="0.8s" /> Villains, I shrieked. <break time="0.8s" /> I admit the deed. <break time="0.8s" /> Tear up the boards. <break time="0.8s" /> Here, here. <break time="0.8s" /> It is the beating. <break time="0.8s" /> Of his terrible heart.
